subject: Gastrointestinal
subtopic: Biliary structures and ampulla of Vater
vignette: A 52-year-old woman presents with right upper quadrant pain, fever, and jaundice. Laboratory studies show an elevated direct bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase, and her amylase and lipase are also markedly elevated. Cholangiography demonstrates a filling defect where the common bile duct and pancreatic duct converge.
question: Obstruction at which of the following sites best explains both the cholangitis and the pancreatitis in this patient?

options.text: Cystic duct
Common hepatic duct
Ampulla of Vater
Main pancreatic duct
Accessory pancreatic duct

explanation_correct: The common bile duct and the main pancreatic duct converge at the ampulla of Vater, where the sphincter of Oddi controls outflow into the duodenum. A gallstone that reaches this confluence can obstruct both ducts simultaneously, producing the "double duct sign" with cholangitis (biliary obstruction) and pancreatitis (pancreatic outflow obstruction). Cholangiography in this patient shows filling defects, the classic appearance of such stones. This single location therefore accounts for both the cholestatic liver injury and the pancreatic enzyme elevation.

explanation_incorrect.A: The cystic duct connects the gallbladder to the common bile duct; a stone there would cause cholecystitis but would not obstruct the common bile duct or the pancreatic duct.
explanation_incorrect.B: The common hepatic duct lies proximal to the confluence with the pancreatic duct, so a stone there would impair bile flow and cause cholangitis but would spare pancreatic drainage.
explanation_incorrect.D: Isolated obstruction of the main pancreatic duct would cause pancreatitis but would not obstruct bile flow, so it would not explain the jaundice and cholangitis.
explanation_incorrect.E: The accessory pancreatic duct drains only a portion of the pancreas into the duodenum separately; obstruction here would not block the common bile duct and cause cholangitis.

educationalObjective: A stone at the ampulla of Vater obstructs both the common bile and pancreatic ducts, producing simultaneous cholangitis and pancreatitis (the double duct sign).

subject: Gastrointestinal
subtopic: Biliary structures and ampulla of Vater
vignette: A 66-year-old man presents with painless jaundice, dark urine, and 8 kg of unintentional weight loss over 3 months. Physical examination reveals a distended, nontender gallbladder. Imaging demonstrates a mass in the head of the pancreas with dilatation of the common bile duct.
question: Which of the following best explains the combination of jaundice and a palpable, nontender gallbladder in this patient?

options.text: Obstruction of the common bile duct by a tumor in the head of the pancreas (Courvoisier sign)
A gallstone impacted in the cystic duct with secondary cholecystitis
Gallstone obstruction at the ampulla of Vater causing cholangitis and pancreatitis
Obstruction of the common hepatic duct above the insertion of the cystic duct
Primary adenocarcinoma of the gallbladder with biliary invasion

explanation_correct: Tumors arising in the head of the pancreas, usually ductal adenocarcinomas, can compress or invade the common bile duct as it passes through the pancreatic head. The resulting painless biliary obstruction causes jaundice, and bile backs up into the gallbladder, which becomes enlarged and nontender. This combination is known as Courvoisier sign and classically points to malignant rather than gallstone obstruction, because chronic gallstone disease typically produces a fibrotic, shrunken gallbladder.

explanation_incorrect.B: A stone in the cystic duct causes cholecystitis with a tender, inflamed gallbladder, not a painless distended one, and would not produce jaundice unless the common bile duct were also blocked.
explanation_incorrect.C: A stone at the ampulla obstructs both bile and pancreatic ducts and causes painful cholangitis and pancreatitis, not the painless jaundice with a distended gallbladder described here.
explanation_incorrect.D: Obstruction of the common hepatic duct proximal to the cystic duct insertion would prevent gallbladder filling with bile, so the gallbladder would not become distended.
explanation_incorrect.E: Primary gallbladder carcinoma is not the classic cause of Courvoisier sign; the enlarged nontender gallbladder with jaundice specifically implicates a pancreatic head tumor obstructing the common bile duct.

educationalObjective: A pancreatic head tumor obstructing the common bile duct produces painless jaundice with an enlarged, nontender gallbladder (Courvoisier sign).

subject: Gastrointestinal
subtopic: Biliary structures and ampulla of Vater
vignette: A 55-year-old woman presents with right upper quadrant pain, fever, and jaundice. Laboratory studies show a conjugated hyperbilirubinemia with elevated alkaline phosphatase, and amylase and lipase are also elevated. Cholangiography reveals a filling defect precisely at the confluence of the common bile duct and the pancreatic duct.
question: Which of the following best characterizes the single obstruction responsible for these findings?

options.text: A stone in the cystic duct producing acute cholecystitis only
A stone in the common hepatic duct producing cholangitis but sparing the pancreas
A pancreatic head tumor producing a shrunken, fibrotic gallbladder
A stone in the main pancreatic duct producing pancreatitis with normal liver enzymes
A stone at the ampulla of Vater producing the double duct sign with cholangitis and pancreatitis

explanation_correct: Because the common bile duct and the main pancreatic duct join at the ampulla of Vater, a stone lodged at that confluence obstructs both outflow tracts. Bile backs up to cause cholangitis with a cholestatic pattern (conjugated bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase), while blocked pancreatic secretions cause pancreatitis with elevated amylase and lipase. This is the double duct sign, and cholangiography shows a filling defect at the point of convergence. No single obstruction at a more proximal or more distal site could produce both abnormalities together.

explanation_incorrect.A: A cystic duct stone causes cholecystitis with right upper quadrant tenderness but would not obstruct either the common bile duct or the pancreatic duct, so jaundice and hyperamylasemia would not occur.
explanation_incorrect.B: The common hepatic duct is proximal to the pancreatic duct confluence, so a stone there would cause cholangitis with jaundice but would leave pancreatic drainage intact and amylase normal.
explanation_incorrect.C: A pancreatic head tumor causes painless jaundice with an enlarged nontender gallbladder (Courvoisier sign), not a shrunken fibrotic gallbladder, and does not typically produce this acute presentation.
explanation_incorrect.D: A stone confined to the main pancreatic duct would elevate amylase and lipase but would not obstruct bile flow, so bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase would remain normal.

educationalObjective: A single stone at the ampulla of Vater simultaneously obstructs the common bile and pancreatic ducts, producing the double duct sign.

subject: Gastrointestinal
subtopic: Biliary structures and ampulla of Vater
vignette: A 44-year-old woman with a history of cholesterol gallstones undergoes cholangiography, which shows filling defects within the gallbladder and within the common bile duct. The surgeon reviews the biliary tree anatomy before planning the procedure.
question: Which duct directly connects the gallbladder to the common hepatic duct to form the common bile duct?

options.text: Main pancreatic duct
Cystic duct
Common hepatic duct
Accessory pancreatic duct
Ampulla of Vater

explanation_correct: The cystic duct drains the gallbladder and joins the common hepatic duct (which carries bile from the liver) to form the common bile duct. The common bile duct then descends behind the pancreatic head and joins the main pancreatic duct at the ampulla of Vater before entering the duodenum through the sphincter of Oddi. Gallstones can therefore be found as filling defects in the gallbladder and in the common bile duct after migrating through the cystic duct.

explanation_incorrect.A: The main pancreatic duct drains pancreatic secretions and joins the common bile duct at the ampulla; it does not connect the gallbladder to the hepatic duct.
explanation_incorrect.C: The common hepatic duct carries bile from the liver and is one of the two ducts that join to form the common bile duct; it is not the gallbladder's outflow tract.
explanation_incorrect.D: The accessory pancreatic duct is a separate pancreatic drainage channel that opens into the duodenum and has no connection to the gallbladder.
explanation_incorrect.E: The ampulla of Vater is the distal confluence of the common bile duct and main pancreatic duct where they empty into the duodenum, not the gallbladder's connection.

educationalObjective: The cystic duct drains the gallbladder and unites with the common hepatic duct to form the common bile duct.
